## Verdict (headline)

Of the four runs this attempt, **exactly one converged: lem-mass-split run A** (claude prover /
codex verifier), root validated + closed, FULL parity with the AISM original. The other three did not
converge and split into two distinct causes:

- **Both reverse-direction runs (mass-split B, starvation B; codex prover / claude verifier) aborted
  `stuck` at exit-12 ×3 with ZERO verdicts applied** — a NEW gap (GAP 11): the claude-opus verifier's
  verdict text fails rk's `extractSingleJsonObject` whole-turn-must-be-one-JSON-object requirement, so
  the verifier's very first (correct) bare-root challenge is discarded 3× and the prover is never
  dispatched. This is validity-relevant and rk-side; NOT fixed here (§7 / L6 → Tier-A escalate).
- **starvation run A (claude prover / codex verifier) aborted `stuck` with 36 of 39 nodes validated
  but root/1.9/1.10 never validated** — a genuine cross-vendor disagreement, NOT an rk bug: the codex
  verifier substantively challenges 1.9 and 1.10 as **incorrect** (category `incorrect`) even after the
  prover re-decomposes them, so no verdict progress → stuck. The machinery worked (43/43 verdicts
  applied, 0 discards, cross-vendor clean on all 36 validated nodes); the workers disagreed on the
  hardest lemma.

The campaign SC4 baseline is now COMPLETE: 6 runs across 3 lemmas × 2 directions, 2,313,435 total live
tokens, 58 validated nodes, 3 converged (whole-lemma) denominators + 1 partial + 2 zero-progress stalls.

## GAP 11 (NEW) — claude-verifier verdict envelope fails rk's whole-turn single-object parse → stuck, 0 progress

**What:** In both reverse-direction runs (claude = verifier), the claude-opus verifier returned a
verdict whose text BEGINS with a well-formed `{"verdict": {"outcome":"challenge", …}}` object but does
not satisfy rk's `extractSingleJsonObject` (src/drive/driver-live.ts:98) — which DELIBERATELY requires
the ENTIRE turn text (after stripping at most one code fence) to `JSON.parse` to exactly one object,
refusing to salvage the "right" `{…}` from a mixed blob because picking wrong could bind a bogus
verdict (a validity semantic). rk's contract (driver-prompts.ts:130) asks for
`{"verdict": {…}, "justification": <string>}`; the opus output evidently carried content around/after
the object (prose, a second object, or a missing/misplaced `justification`) that the conservative
extractor will not accept. Result: exit 12 (`parse-failed`) → node-skipped (`worker exit 12`) → 3
rounds no progress → `stuck` (exit 4), ZERO verdicts applied, prover never dispatched.

**Why it matters (L6 / §7):** a legitimate verifier challenge is silently discarded and the run aborts
with no progress and NO reprompt/repair path. Validity-relevant (what a verifier is allowed to certify,
and truthful handling of its verdict). Whether the fix is parser-side (accept the `{"verdict":…,
"justification":…}` envelope more robustly / add a single bounded reprompt) or prompt-side (tighten the
claude verifier's output discipline) is genuinely ambiguous (L5: the strictness is a deliberate
validity choice, but the effect reads rk-bug-flavored) → Tier-A escalate, top-tier review before any
fix. NOT fixed here. Direction-specific (codex-verifier direction parses fine and converged/progressed
in all three run-A runs), content/variance dependent (weighted-min run B converged).

**Observability limitation (candidate bead):** rk persists only a bounded ~400-char snippet of the
parse-failed rawText, truncated mid-`reason`, so a triage cannot see from the banked evidence whether
the failure was trailing prose, a preamble, a second object, or a mid-string escape. Persisting the
full rawText (or a larger bound) on a parse-failed that leads to a stuck-abort would make GAP 11
diagnosable without a re-run.

## starvation run A non-convergence — genuine disagreement, not an rk bug

The codex verifier challenges 1.9 and 1.10 with category `incorrect` (a substantive correctness
objection, NOT the `missing`/`dependency`-content shape of the fixed GAP 10). The claude prover
re-decomposes each into 14 / 12 children that all validate, but the PARENT inference is re-challenged
`incorrect` again → no progress on 1.9/1.10 → stuck. All machinery worked (43/43 applied, 0 discards,
cross-vendor clean). This is the honest SC4 finding on the hardest lemma: under the current per-node
protocol, opus's granular decomposition (39 nodes vs AISM's 7) does not satisfy the codex hostile
verifier on this rank-three-idempotent non-existence obstruction, and the protocol has no mechanism to
force the parent inference past a repeated substantive objection. Candidate P2 bead (protocol, not
validity-machinery): a parent re-challenged `incorrect` after its children validate should either
converge (the prover must ADDRESS the specific objection, not just re-decompose) or fail more cheaply
than 5 turns / ~185k tokens per stalled parent.

  parse-failed that leads to stuck-abort, persist the full rawText so GAP 11 is diagnosable without a

  verifier's specific objection. The current protocol has no "address-the-objection" path distinct from

## One-line recommendation (for TJO / M3.9)

The SC4 baseline is COMPLETE (33,004 tok/validated-node pooled over the 3 converged whole-lemma runs;
~0.50 vs ~0.93 per-direction cache split is the M3.9 caching lever) — but the reverse (claude-verifier)
direction now has a NEW Tier-A blocker (GAP 11) that stalls it at zero progress on 2 of 3 lemmas, and
the hardest lemma does not converge in EITHER direction under the current protocol. Land GAP 11 (with
review) and revisit the starvation "incorrect" re-challenge protocol before any SC4 improvement work
leans on the reverse-direction numbers.
